universes.title: Known Space
universes.author: Larry Niven
universes.blurb: Niven's future-history setting deliberately used real nearby stars for its earliest slower-than-light colonies — the constant-acceleration slowboat era this app's own trip engine already models. Check which colonies to visit and reorder them below to build your own route.

stars.citation: Colonized circa 2091 in the Alpha Centauri system (Niven's text doesn't specify component A vs B; mapped here to Rigil Kentaurus, Alpha Centauri A) — larryniven.fandom.com/wiki/Wunderland
Colony world orbiting Procyon, ~11.3 ly from Sol — the colony ship crash-landed, giving the world its name — larryniven.fandom.com/wiki/We_Made_It
Colony world in the Sirius system — larryniven.fandom.com/wiki/Known_Space
Colony world orbiting Tau Ceti — larryniven.fandom.com/wiki/Known_Space

universes.title: Project Hail Mary
universes.author: Andy Weir
universes.blurb: Grace's full arc across the book, both real stars he actually travels to.

stars.citation: Astrophage's home system, orbiting the real star Tau Ceti, ~11.9 ly from Sol — space.com/entertainment/space-movies-shows/i-talked-to-andy-weir-about-the-astrobiology-behind-project-hail-mary
40 Eridani A — IAU name Keid, ~16 ly from Sol — Rocky's home star; Grace ends the book living there — projecthailmary.fandom.com/wiki/Rocky

routes.title: Sol → Tau Ceti → Erid
routes.citation: Grace's complete journey: the Hail Mary flies Sol→Tau Ceti alone to find a cure for astrophage; at the book's climax he turns back to rescue Rocky's dying ship and accompanies him home to Erid, where he stays — two legs of one real arc, not a single unbroken flight path.
